## Paragraph Skeletons

### Skeleton A — Quantified Control Variable Enumeration
**Slots:**
1. "X should be equal to N unit"
2. "Each [container] should have N unit of [substance] mixed and dissolved in it"
3. "[dimensions] has to be filled with N of [substrate]"
4. "N [organism] per [container]"
5. "All [subjects] should be exposed to the same [A] and [B]."
**Fill:** List 3–5 quantified controls; close with uniform-exposure statement.
**Original:** "The amount of water in each molar solution should be equal to one cup." … "All of the plants should be exposed to the same light source and temperature."
**Demo:** "The volume of buffer in each reaction tube should be equal to 2 mL." / "Each tube should have 0.5 mL of enzyme solution mixed and diluted in it." / "Each 10 mL cuvette has to be filled with 3 mL of substrate." / "One substrate concentration per cuvette." / "All of the cuvettes should be exposed to the same incubation time and temperature."

### Skeleton B — Grouped Materials List
**Slots:** Ordered noun phrases with quantities. Group: liquids → powders → branded preparations → tools → glassware → hardware → PPE → containers → biologicals → instruments.
**Fill:** Use exact grouping order; quantify each item with units.
**Original:** "1000ml Sterile Water" / "Murashige and Skoog Medium 5L" / "1 1000 ml beaker" / "1 Pressure cooker at 17 psi" / "1 pair of gloves" / "30 pots 1 pt of soil" / "30 seeds of brassica rapa" / "1 balance."
**Demo:** "500 mL distilled water" / "5 g sodium bicarbonate" / "1.0 mL bromothymol blue indicator" / "1 dissolved oxygen probe, calibrated" / "1 1000 mL beaker" / "1 LED light source at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800 lux" / "1 pair of gloves" / "5 250 mL bottles, filled with 200 mL water" / "5 sprigs of Elodea, 5 cm each" / "1 light meter."

### Skeleton C — Safety + Setup Imperative
**Slots:** Paired safety imperatives (compound verb+PPE; hair+secondary PPE), then labelling block (verb+numbers+grid geometry+tool alternative+placement).
**Fill:** Open with two-sentence safety pair; follow with single-sentence grid specification.
**Original:** "Gather materials and put on gloves. Tie up hair and make sure to wear closed toe shoes. Label each row of pots with the numbers 1-5, corresponding to each row that the pots are on. Each row should have 7 pots and 5 pots per column. Masking tape and/or a permanent marker can be used. Place them in a wide area that has access to light."
**Demo:** "Gather materials and put on gloves. Tie up hair and make sure to wear a lab coat. Label each Petri dish with the numbers 1-6, corresponding to each pH solution. Each dish should have 10 seeds and 5 dishes per treatment group. Pipettes and/or disposable droppers can be used. Place them in a controlled area that has access to a 25 °C incubator."

### Skeleton D — Mix → Correct → Condition → Troubleshoot
**Slots:** S1 measure+add solvent+solute at condition; S2 rinse corrective ("to remove trace residues of …"); S3 add supplements + dissolution imperative; S4 conditional rescue with three coordinated verbs + visual success criterion.
**Fill:** Follow exact sentence sequence; rescue clause requires three comma-separated verbs.
**Original:** "Take 600 ml of distilled water and add 4.54 grams of dehydrated Murashige and Skoog medium at room temperature (15-30 C). Rinse the media via with a small quantity of distilled water to remove trace residues of powder. Add the desired heat stable supplements prior to pressure cooking. Continue stirring until the powder has completely dissolved. If the powder does not completely dissolve then use HCL and mix, heat, and rotate until the solution becomes clear."
**Demo:** "Pour 100 mL of distilled water and add 1 g of agar powder at room temperature (20-25 °C). Rinse the flask with a small quantity of distilled water to remove trace residues of powder. Add the desired indicator dye prior to autoclaving. Continue swirling until the agar has completely suspended. If the agar does not completely suspend then use a magnetic stirrer and heat, stir, and rotate until the solution becomes translucent."

### Skeleton E — Numbered Procedure with Embedded Parameters
**Slots:** (1) vessel+material imperative; (2) sterilise (temp+time+pressure ceiling); (3) fixed-volume dosing with spatial targeting; (4) solution prep (mass+volume+temp+saturation); (5) graduated dose ladder; (6) homogenise; (7) subject at fixed density; (8) maintain (interval+volume); (9) duration; (10) count+measure DVs; (11) disposal.
**Fill:** Maintain imperative voice; embed all parameters in parentheses or inline.
**Original:** "Dispense the mediums into suitable closed containers. Pressure cook at 121-125 C for about 15-20 minutes, never over 20 psi. Evenly pour 10ml of the solution into each pot of soil. Take the bottle of lauric acid, and pour 25 grams into 5 into 1200 ml of water heated to 37 C. Mix until the lauric acid is saturated. Pour 10 ml each into the second row… 20 ml… 30 ml… 40 ml. Stir the dirt. Plant 1 seed per pot. Every two days, water the plants with 300 ml. Observe for 45 days. Observe how many new seedlings… Measure the length of the roots and stem. Safely discard and clean up lab materials."
**Demo:** "Dispense Hoagland's solution into 250 ml Erlenmeyer flasks and autoclave at 121 °C for 15 minutes, never above 20 psi. Pipette 10 ml of sterile medium into each well of a 24-well plate. Weigh 0.5 g of NaCl into 500 ml of medium warmed to 25 °C. Mix until fully dissolved. Add 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 mM NaCl to columns 1–5. Vortex the plate. Transfer 3 Lemna minor fronds per well. Every two days, replace the medium with 5 ml fresh solution. Record for 14 days. Count frond number and measure total frond area. Safely discard and clean up lab materials."

### Skeleton F — Mass-into-Volume-at-Temperature with Saturation Endpoint
**Slots:** (1) "Take the bottle of X"; (2) "pour N unit into V unit of [solvent] heated to T °C"; (3) "Mix until the [solute] is [endpoint word] in the [solvent]."
**Fill:** Three sentences exactly; endpoint word varies by dissolution state.
**Original:** "Take the bottle of lauric acid, and pour 25 grams into 5 into 1200 ml of water heated to 37 C. Mix until the lauric acid is saturated in the water."
**Demo:** "Take the bottle of boric acid, and pour 4 grams into 200 ml of distilled water heated to 60 °C. Mix until the boric acid is fully dissolved."

### Skeleton G — Graduated Dose Distribution with Closing Homogenisation
**Slots:** (1) control-row dose ("Pour N ml into [row/column]"); (2) escalating comma-chain ("Then pour N into [row+1], N into [row+2], and N into [row+3]"); (3) one-verb substrate-mixing close.
**Fill:** Escalating values in comma-chain; final verb applies to entire substrate.
**Original:** "Pour 10 ml each into the second row of pots. Then pour 20 ml of the solution into the third row, 30ml each pot for the fourth row, and 40ml each pot for the fifth row. Stir the dirt."
**Demo:** "Pour 5 ml of distilled water into column 1. Then pour 10 ml of the 10 mM solution into column 2, 15 ml into column 3, and 20 ml into column 4. Agitate the agar."

### Skeleton H — Maintenance Schedule with Explicit Duration
**Slots:** (1) "Every N days"; (2) "[verb] the [subject] with V unit for each [unit]"; (3) "Repeat the process of [verb]-ing and observe for N days."
**Fill:** Interval + volume per unit + total observation period.
**Original:** "Every two days, water the plants with 300 ml for each plant. Repeat the process of watering and observe for 45 days."
**Demo:** "Every three days, feed the Daphnia with 2 ml of algal suspension for each beaker. Repeat the process of feeding and observe for 21 days."

### Skeleton I — Equipment Commissioning Unit
**Slots:** (1) Device-to-interface connection (imperative); (2) Parameter setting (colon + numeric value + parenthetical rationale).
**Fill:** Any instrument needing controllable setting; maintain imperative voice.
**Original:** "Connect the colorimeter to the laptop and initiate the data logging software. / Set the wavelength: 635 nm (red colour)."
**Demo:** "Connect the conductivity probe to the datalogger and launch the recording software. / Set the sampling rate: 1 Hz (to capture rapid ion‑movement changes)."

### Skeleton J — Calibration Unit
**Slots:** Transfer blank medium into vessel; use it to calibrate instrument. (semicolon construction)
**Fill:** Specify blank, holder, action.
**Original:** "Transfer distilled water into a cuvette; use it to calibrate the colorimeter."
**Demo:** "Transfer pure solvent into the sample cell; use it to zero the spectrophotometer."

### Skeleton K — Mixture-Construction Unit (dependency-chained transfers)
**Slots:** (1) Transfer environment reagent(s) into container; (2) Transfer variable reagent (with backward reference "from Step X"); (3) Transfer indicator (with tool).
**Fill:** Preserve order and backward reference; each transfer names reagent, volume, tool.
**Original:** "Transfer 0.5 mL 1.0 M H₂SO₄(aq) + 0.5 mL H₂O₂ into a beaker. / Transfer 1.0 mL of the 0.0002 M KI solution from Step 2b. / Transfer 1.0 mL of Starch solution into the mixture using a dropping pipette."
**Demo:** "Transfer 2.0 mL 0.1 M HCl(aq) + 1.0 mL Na₂S₂O₃ into a flask. / Transfer 0.5 mL of the 0.005 M Pb(NO₃)₂ solution from Step 2a. / Transfer 1.0 mL of KI indicator into the mixture using a graduated pipette."

### Skeleton L — Measurement + Replication + Sweep Unit
**Slots:** (1) Insert vessel, initiate data collection at parameter; (2) Repeat steps (range) N more times for N trials; (3) Repeat steps (range) whilst changing independent variable (list values).
**Fill:** Single read → replicate → vary; order fixed.
**Original:** "Insert the cuvette into the colorimeter and initiate data collection at 635 nm. / Repeat Steps 5–8 two more times to get three trials of absorbance recording. / Repeat Steps 3–8, whilst changing the concentration of KI solution (0.0004, 0.0006, …)."
**Demo:** "Insert the vial into the fluorometer and initiate data logging at 520 nm. / Repeat Steps 4–7 two more times to obtain three trials of fluorescence intensity. / Repeat Steps 2–7, whilst changing the enzyme concentration (0.10, 0.20, 0.40 mg mL⁻¹, …)."

### Skeleton M — Controlled-Condition Soaking/Setup Block
**Slots:** (1) phase heading; (2) sample mass + tool + qualitative observation; (3) solvent volume + transfer; (4) sample subdivision + container assembly; (5) environmental placement with control bracket; (6) calibration interval + stopwatch precision; (7) IV application + timing precision; (8) replication total; (9) IV cascade.
**Fill:** State substrate, mass, solvent, control temp, IV, replication count.
**Original:** "Measure 20.0g of dry seaweed… Place the beaker in the pre-setup water bath at 25° C (Room Temperature; Control Setup)… Leave the sample in the water bath for a period of 0 hours controlled using a stopwatch (±0.05s)… Repeat Steps 1–4 9 more times to obtain a total of 10 trials per conditions."
**Demo:** "Measure 15.0 g of dried kidney beans using an electronic balance and weighing boat. Note the bean's outer colour. Transfer 100.0 mL of sodium bicarbonate buffer into a 250 mL beaker. Divide into 5 equal portions and submerge. Place in a pre-set water bath at 20 °C (Room Temperature; Control Setup) and calibrate for 30 s. Leave for 0 minutes. Repeat Steps 1–4 nine more times for 10 trials per condition."

### Skeleton N — Post-Treatment Disruption + Homogenization Block
**Slots:** (1) sample retrieval; (2) discard residual liquid; (3) mechanical disruption tool + rep count + mechanism clause ("to [verb] [structure] and release [analyte]"); (4) transfer to blender; (5) measured diluent volume; (6) timed blending interval + stopwatch; (7) labelled storage beaker.
**Fill:** Retrieve solid, discard solvent, crush/grind with mechanism clause, blend, label.
**Original:** "Obtain the different samples and discard any liquid remaining… crush the sample using a pestle (10 times) to ease the breakdown of cellular components and release the remaining iodine… Blend for 15 seconds controlled using a stopwatch… Transfer blended samples into separate beaker and label 'Blended Seaweed'."
**Demo:** "Remove each bean sample and pour off remaining buffer. Grind in a mortar with a pestle (12 strokes) to rupture the seed coat and release soluble sugars. Transfer to blender. Add 80 mL distilled water. Blend for 20 seconds controlled using a stopwatch. Decant into a labelled beaker marked 'Blended Bean Extract'."

### Skeleton O — Reagent-Build-Up + Instrumental-Read Block
**Slots:** (1) retrieve labelled sample from prior segment; (2) separation method; (3) cuvette reagent build-up in fixed chemical order (reagent 1 + volume + tool → reagent 2 + volume + tool → analyte + volume + tool → indicator + volume + tool); (4) instrument + named wavelength + recording; (5) cascading replication across IV levels and second IV.
**Fill:** Retrieve extract, filter, add reagents in chemical order, insert instrument, record, replicate.
**Original:** "Obtain the blended sample… Extract the liquid using a strainer… Transfer 0.5mL H₂SO₄ + 0.5mL H₂O₂… Transfer 2.0 mL of the liquid… Transfer 0.5 mL of the starch indicator… Insert the cuvette in the colorimeter and measure absorbance at 635nm… Record… Repeat Steps 1–4… 1–5… 1–6 for the other temperature condition (80°C)."
**Demo:** "Obtain the blended bean extract from Part Two. Strain through muslin. Obtain a dry cuvette; transfer 0.5 mL DNS reagent + 0.5 mL NaOH, then 1.0 mL strained extract using a dropping pipette, then 0.5 mL glucose indicator. Insert into spectrophotometer and measure absorbance at 540 nm. Record. Repeat Steps 1–4 for each soaking-time condition, then 1–5 for other times, then 1–6 for the second temperature (70 °C)."

### Skeleton P — Serial Dilution Step
**Slots:** tool; X ml; previous conc (Treatment N); Y ml water; mixing time; Z% result.
**Fill:** Tool matching volume; previous % + reference; X+Y constant; same mixing; Z = (X/(X+Y))*prev%.
**Original:** "using a 50 ml graduated cylinder 20 ml of the 0.5% solution (treatment 3) were taken and poured into an erlenmeyer flask containing 80 ml of water, the solution was then stored for 30 seconds by hand resulting in a concentration 0.1%."
**Demo:** "using a 25 ml volumetric pipette 25 ml of the 2.0 M stock (Preparation 3) were transferred into a volumetric flask containing 75 ml of distilled water, the solution was then inverted for 30 seconds resulting in a concentration 0.5 M."

### Skeleton Q — Stock Preparation
**Slots:** tool; X ml; raw material (species); Y ml solvent; mixing time.
**Fill:** Smallest accurate tool; name raw material; Y so X+Y round; mixing time consistent.
**Original:** "using a pipette 0.5 ml of the microalgae concentrated extract C. zofingiensis was dissolved in an erlenmeyer flask containing 100 ml of water then stirred for 30 seconds by hand."
**Demo:** "using a micropipette 1.0 ml of the saffron concentrated extract Crocus sativus was dissolved in a beaker containing 99 ml of ethanol then agitated for 30 seconds by hand."

### Skeleton R — IV/DV Enumeration
**Slots:** IV name (noun phrase, species in parentheses), IV levels (parenthetical list of 3), DV measures (two noun phrases joined by "and", each with unit).
**Fill:** Choose manipulated factor, three doses, one morphometric + one mass.
**Original:** "Independent variables: concentrations of microalgae (Chlorella zofingiensis) extract (0.5%, 0.1%, 0.01%). Dependent variable: the height (cm) and the fresh weight (gr)."
**Demo:** "Independent variables: salinity of irrigation water (NaCl at 0 mM, 50 mM, 100 mM). Dependent variable: the root length (cm) and the dry mass (mg) of *Lactuca sativa* seedlings."

### Skeleton S — Controlled Variables List
**Slots:** delivery; substrate + source; volume per time over duration; equal duration; replicates per group + total.
**Fill:** Five-item semicolon list; identical duration for all groups.
**Original:** "Irrigation; amount of water applied…10 ml per week over 3 weeks—experiment identical—10 repetitions per treatment; overall 50 plants."
**Demo:** "Mist application; Hoagland solution pH 6.0; 5 ml foliar spray every 48 h over 14 days; duration identical at 21 days; 8 plants per treatment, total 32."

### Skeleton T — Apparatus Enumeration
**Slots:** workspace; subjects (count, stage); solvent; treatment 1 (volume, species, provider, credential); treatment 2; bulk vessels; precise tools ±; application; recording; substrate; pots (volume); accessories; measurement ±; handling; closing tool.
**Fill:** Use-order as above; attach ± to tools, credential to inputs.
**Original:** "An irrigation table with irrigation system. 55 leaf celery seedlings. Tap water. 50 ml concentrated brown algae extract (U. pinnatifida); provided by Dr. Eran Barak which specializes in Innovative Plant Nutrition. 50 ml concentrated microalgae extract (C. zofingiensis); provided by Dr. Eran Barak. Two 250 ml glass beakers. Five 200 ml erlenmeyer flasks. 100 ml graduated cylinder ± 0.5 ml. Two 1 ml glass pipette ±0.05 ml. 10 ml syringe ± 0.25ml. A notebook and a pan. Soil provided by the greenhouse. 55 pots ~500 ml. Plastic cap, scissors. 30 cm ruler ± 0.05 cm. Electric scale ± 0.1 gr (no label). Large basket, gardening shovel. 50 ml graduated cylinder 0.5 ± ml."
**Demo:** "Climate-controlled chamber with LED. 36 *Drosophila melanogaster* pupae. Distilled water. 20 ml 1 mM caffeine; provided by Dr. R. Singh, chronobiology. 20 ml 0.1% ethanol vehicle; provided by Dr. R. Singh. Three 100 ml beakers. Two 50 ml Erlenmeyer flasks. 25 ml graduated cylinder ± 0.5 ml. One 1 ml micropipette ± 0.01 ml. Soft-tipped applicator. Stereo microscope, lab notebook. Instant *Drosophila* medium. 36 vials 30 ml. Foam plugs, cotton buds. Digital caliper ± 0.01 mm. Analytical balance ± 0.001 g (no model). Transfer pipettes, sorting brush. 10 ml graduated cylinder ± 0.1 ml."

### Skeleton U — Interview: Origin-and-Driver Turn-Taking
**Slots:** (1) interviewer opener (greeting + thanks + purpose + transition); (2) personal-driver clause (first-person plural + present-tense self-description); (3) market-gap clause (causal connector + first-person plural + past-tense motivation + target market phrase).
**Fill:** Probe origin → personal passion → market justification.
**Original:** "Good Afternoon Mr. Tejas. Thanks for giving time for this meeting. This meeting is regarding my Business Management Research Paper. First off, lest start with your business, Kreme De La Kreme. How did you come up with the idea to start a business?" / "My Wife and I are fanatics of Gelato ourselves." / "So, we wanted to bring quality Gelato to people in Mumbai."
**Demo:** "Good afternoon Ms. Rao. Thanks for taking the time to speak with me. This conversation is for my IB Business Management internal assessment. First off, let's begin with your startup, EcoPack Solutions. How did you come up with the idea to start a business?" / "My co-founder and I were frustrated by single-use plastic on our campus." / "So, we wanted to bring compostable packaging to small cafés in Bengaluru."

### Skeleton V — Interview: Threshold-then-Comparison Q-A Pair
**Slots:** (1) capital/method question; (2) sources + liability qualifier; (3) break-even projection; (4) comparative probe; (5) past-vs-present figures.
**Fill:** Funding method → start/end trajectory → break-even benchmark.
**Original:** "What method(s) did you use to fund this project?" / "Apart from our personal savings, we took a loan, which we are yet to repay." / "We expect that we would need monthly sales of about 300,000 INR per month to break even." / "So, what were your sales like when you started, and how is it now?" / "We started with 80,000 INR per month, and are at about 180,000 to 200,000 INR per month now."
**Demo:** "What method(s) did you use to staff your kitchen?" / "Apart from two family members who manage shifts, we hired one pastry chef on contract, whom we are still onboarding." / "We expect that we would need roughly 150 covers per day to break even on labour." / "So, what was your daily footfall when you opened, and how is it now?" / "We started with about 40 covers a day, and are at about 90 to 110 covers a day now."

### Skeleton W — Interview: Core-Product-Unpack-then-Complementary-Range
**Slots:** (1) core claim ("mainly offer [core], which is [made/controlled] in-house"); (2) human-capital unpack ("We have a [role] who [action] all the [components]"); (3) complementary enumeration (comma-then-final-and list); (4) B2B channel ("We [wholesale action] the [item] in bulk to [B2B partner] who [resell]").
**Fill:** Core → control mechanism → complementary SKUs → wholesale channel.
**Original:** "We mainly offer different flavors of gelato, which is made in-house." / "We have a professional chef who develops all the flavors and recipes." / "We also sell sundaes, shakes, cookies, waffles, and brownies." / "We sell the brownies in bulk to another local café who sell it at their outlets."
**Demo:** "We mainly offer single-origin pour-over coffee, which is brewed in-house." / "We have a head roaster who sources and profiles all the beans." / "We also sell espresso, filter coffee, cold brew, croissants, and banana bread." / "We sell the banana bread in bulk to a nearby co-working space that resells it at their pantry."

### Skeleton X — Confounding-Fix
**Slots:** As [X] are relative to [Y], the data had to be [verb]ed. This was done by [operation] for each [unit].
**Fill:** Identify hidden variable; state transformation needed; define operation + denominator.
**Original:** "As the cases of malaria are relative to the population of the country, the data had to be standardized. This was done by calculating the incidence of malaria per 100,000 people for each year."
**Demo:** "As CO₂ emissions are relative to each economy's size, the data had to be normalized. This was done by calculating emissions per million USD of GDP for each country for each year."

### Skeleton Y — Data Table Caption + Rows
**Slots:** **Table N: Raw data for [variable] (in [unit]) per [grain]** — Rows: [Entity] [t1] … [tn]
**Fill:** Variable + unit + time grain; entity in first column; chronological measurements across.
**Original:** "**Table 3: Raw data for forest land (in hectares) per year**" with Peru … Zimbabwe.
**Demo:** "**Table 7: Raw data for daily step count (in steps) per week**" with Patient 01 … Patient 13.

### Skeleton Z — Risk-Tail + Mitigation
**Slots:** [Citation] as well as [secondary risk] (Citation). In order to avoid the risks mentioned the use of [protection category] such as [concrete item 1] as well as the [repeated action 2] were utilized.
**Fill:** Next hazard + citation; convert to purpose clause; name category + object + behavior.
**Original:** "(Jakuboski, 2015) as well as heatstroke and dehydration … In order to avoid the risks mentioned the use of protection measures such as hats and sunscreen as well as the repeated drinking of water were utilized."
**Demo:** "(ScienceDirect, 2020) as well as chemical burns from sodium hydroxide splashes. In order to avoid the risks mentioned the use of protective equipment such as safety goggles and lab coats as well as the repeated rinsing of the workstation were performed."

### Skeleton AA — Blanket-Ethics + Authority
**Slots:** Ethical and environmental: [flat negative claim covering three categories] was imposed on [category 1], [category 2] or [category 3] during the course of this investigation. The investigation was planned according to [authority name] [year].
**Fill:** Doubled-negative blanket claim; exactly three nouns ascending scope; cite institutional guideline.
**Original:** "Ethical and environmental: no intentional or unintentional harm was imposed on humans, animals or the environment … The investigation was planned according to IB ethical and safety guidelines."
**Demo:** "Ethical and environmental: no direct or indirect distress was caused to participants, data or the school setting during the course of this investigation. The study was designed in accordance with BPS ethical guidelines for research with minors (2018)."
